---
title: "How political alliances shape trade and welfare in Europe"
description: "Research with Karen Jackson finds NATO membership significantly boosts exports, and that expansion to Finland, Sweden, and Ukraine would benefit EU economies."
date: "2024-11-18"
categories: [trade-wars, political-economy]
---

Written with Karen Jackson, this post sets out research on how military
alliances like NATO shape European trade and welfare beyond their security
role. The findings show that NATO membership significantly boosts members'
exports, that extending the alliance to Finland, Sweden, and Ukraine would
benefit EU economies, and — strikingly — that smaller nations' NATO accession
looks close to "self-financing," since the trade gains offset the cost of
higher defence spending commitments. A US withdrawal from NATO or the
alliance's collapse, by contrast, would impose substantial economic costs on
Europe.

**Originally published on LSE EUROPP (European Politics and Policy blog)**, November 18, 2024.
